current_bottleneck: There is now a clean coordinate tradeoff. 631a/629a encoded-increment generation preserves anchor-factor and IV-factor joint behavior but accumulates IV level drift/explosions. 638a level-score generation fixes IV support/tails/cross-cell structure but damages anchor-factor changes and joint co-movement. last_result_summary: 638a implemented a state-conditioned level-score transition: same level+increment conditioning as 631a, but samples next empirical level-score changes and derives encoded increments by differencing generated levels. Tests passed. IV score was 4/11, passing surface, time_series, block_ar, and cross_cell_correlation. Surface explosion fell to 0.0%, kurtosis ratio was 0.940, q99 tail-scale passed 22/25, cross-cell corr/rank was 0.998/1.316, and pathwise q90/q99 ratios passed at 0.733/0.896. But coverage was 69.7%, conditionality MAE reduction 4.3%, level KS 6/25, median-bias 9/25, mean-reversion active cells 7/12, and pathwise KS 0.555. Joint-panel audit worsened: factor KS mean 0.156, q99 pass 6/13, factor-factor gen abs corr 0.052 vs GT 0.225, IV-factor gen abs corr 0.073 vs GT 0.149.
next_step_recommendation: Do post-experiment analysis/ideation before code. Decide whether a single architecture with spec-driven generated coordinates is principled: support-valid level-score generation for IV-like mean-reverting level variables and increment generation for random-walk-like anchor variables, while retaining one shared memory/transition and one joint likelihood/training path.
